deep.reconstruction:
Problem (heading 'Allgemeine Umkehrung der Reihen', general reversion of series). Given p^m = Q := q^n + a q^{n+ν} + b q^{n+2ν} + c q^{n+3ν} + ... = q^n(1 + a q^ν + b q^{2ν} + ...), express q^θ as a series in powers of p.

Step 1 (substitution). Put x = q^ν, f(x) = (1 + a x + b x^2 + c x^3 + ...)^{-ν/n}, u = p^{νm/n}. Raising p^m = q^n(1+ax+...) to the power ν/n gives p^{mν/n} = x(1+ax+...)^{ν/n}. So x = u f(x), and the target is q^θ = x^{θ/ν} = u^{θ/ν} f(x)^{θ/ν}. In Gauss's notation 'fx^λ' means (f(x))^λ.

Step 2 (Lagrange's theorem). Embed the equation in x = t + u f(x) and expand in u. Gauss writes
f(x)^λ = f(t)^λ + λu/(λ+1)·d f(t)^{λ+1}/dt + λu^2/((λ+2)·2!)·d^2 f(t)^{λ+2}/dt^2 + λu^3/((λ+3)·3!)·d^3 f(t)^{λ+3}/dt^3 + ...
This holds with t = 0 after differentiation, i.e. for x = u f(x).
Justification (mine). By Lagrange, [u^k] H(x) = (1/k)[t^{k-1}] H'(t) f(t)^k. Take H = f^λ, so H' f^k = λ f^{λ+k-1} f' = λ/(λ+k)·(f^{λ+k})'. Hence [u^k] f(x)^λ = λ/(λ+k)·[t^k] f(t)^{λ+k}.
Gauss restates this in coefficient form:
f(x)^λ = Σ_k λu^k/(λ+k) · Coeff_{t^k} f(t)^{λ+k}.

Step 3 (change of variable). The dummy t may be replaced by q^ν. Then f(q^ν) = (Q/q^n)^{-ν/n} = q^ν Q^{-ν/n}, so f(q^ν)^{λ+k} = q^{ν(λ+k)} Q^{-(λ+k)ν/n}. Its coefficient of q^{kν} equals the coefficient of q^{-νλ} in Q^{-(λ+k)ν/n}. Hence
f(x)^λ = Σ_k λu^k/(λ+k) · Coeff_{q^{-νλ}} Q^{-(λ+k)ν/n}.

Step 4. Set λ = θ/ν and multiply by u^{θ/ν}:
q^θ = Σ_k θ/(θ+kν) · u^{(θ+kν)/ν} · Coeff_{q^{-θ}} Q^{-(θ+kν)/n}, with u^{(θ+kν)/ν} = p^{m(θ+kν)/n}.
The next page restates this as [p^μ] q^θ = (θm)/(μn) · Coeff_{q^{-θ}} Q^{-μ/m}, where μ = m(θ+kν)/n. This is a coefficient-extraction ('residue') form of the Lagrange–Bürmann inversion formula, valid for fractional leading exponents.

Check of normalization (mine). For Q = q^n the formula gives q^θ = p^{θm/n}, as it should.
errors: In the first bracketed q^ν-form (second line), the third term is written with prefactor λu/(λ+1). It should be λu²/(λ+2), as in the lines before and after.
In the last displayed line, the exponent of Q in the third term appears as -(θ+2ν)/ν. It should be -(θ+2ν)/n, which is how the next page has it.
The term 'Coeff q^0' (first term of the q^ν-form) is correct only because f(q^ν)^λ = q^{νλ}Q^{-λν/n}. This shift of exponents is implicit, not a slip.

Lagrange's series is stated without the qualification about convergence or formal-power-series validity. It is also only valid as written at t=0 (as Gauss notes), not for general t. These are minor and not errors in the formal sense.

results.what: Expansion of f(x)^λ, where x = u f(x), as Σ λ u^k/(λ+k) [t^k] f(t)^{λ+k}
results.modern_name: Lagrange inversion theorem / Lagrange–Bürmann formula (power form)

results.what: Reversion of p^m = q^n(1 + a q^ν + ...) giving the coefficient of p^μ in q^θ as (θm/(μn))·[q^{-θ}] Q^{-μ/m}
results.modern_name: Coefficient-extraction (residue) form of Lagrange inversion; generalized series reversion with fractional exponents
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (Crelle 6, 1830, 'De resolutione aequationum per series infinitas'); Cauchy (residue form, 1826)

deep.surprise_reason: Using Lagrange inversion was standard by 1800, so that part is routine for Gauss. The neat 'coefficient of q^{-θ} in Q^{-μ/m}' form, and its 'pars absoluta' variant on the next page, anticipates Jacobi's 1830 residue-type formulation. If the page dates near 1809, as the bundle name suggests, this is a mildly notable unpublished anticipation. It is not a major new result.

Instance of the next-page restatement [p^μ] q^θ = θm/(μn)·[q^{-θ}] Q^{-μ/m}. Here [q^{-θ}] Q^{-μ/m} = [q^{kν}](1+aq+...)^{-nμ/m... } reduces to [q^k](1+a q)^{-(θ+kν)/n}. Compare with a direct reversion of p^2 = q^3(1+aq).

transcription_corrections: Second bracketed line: the image indeed shows the prefactor λu/(λ+1) (Gauss's slip); the intended prefactor is λuu/(λ+2).
Last line: the third term ends with 'Coeff q^{-θ}' (cut off at the page edge), not 'Coeff q'. The exponent of Q is written -(θ+2ν)/ν in the manuscript (a slip for /n).
Last line first factor: 'u^{θ/ν}' (Gauss overwrote the u), correctly transcribed.
